new_task_1.title: Make `VersionInfo` hashable by version value
new_task_1.description: The upgrade adds `VersionInfo.__hash__`, making `attr.VersionInfo` instances hashable using their version components so equal version values produce the same hash.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `attr.VersionInfo` behaves as a hashable immutable version value after upgrading to 25.4.0, so callers can hash instances and use equal version descriptors interchangeably in hashed collections.

expectation.grounded: `attr.VersionInfo` must implement `__hash__` by hashing the tuple `(year, minor, micro, releaselevel)`. Instances with the same four component values should therefore produce the same hash and be accepted anywhere Python requires a hashable object.
expectation.conceptual: VersionInfo objects should behave like stable value objects: if two instances describe the same release, they should hash the same and work in sets, dictionaries, and other hash-based uses.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing comparison semantics or the component fields that define a version. Limit the observable change to adding hash support derived from the existing version components.
constraints.conceptual: Keep VersionInfo's ordering and equality behavior intact; the upgrade should only add consistent hashing for the already-defined version value.

behavior: `hash(VersionInfo(...))` now succeeds instead of relying on the object being unhashable.
Two `VersionInfo` instances with identical `year`, `minor`, `micro`, and `releaselevel` values produce the same hash.
The hash is derived from the full version identity tuple `(year, minor, micro, releaselevel)`.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller computes `hash(VersionInfo(19, 2, 0, "final"))`, the call should succeed.
When two `VersionInfo` instances have the same `year`, `minor`, `micro`, and `releaselevel`, their hashes should be equal.
When a `VersionInfo` instance is used as a dictionary key or set element, Python should treat it as a hashable value object.
